newsitem.title: ECUADOR: President says poll to strengthen Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: President says poll to strengthen Ecuador.

text.p: Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon said on Monday a popular poll he has proposed to gauge the legitimacy of his government will strengthen democracy and his administration.

The non-binding May 25 poll will put 13 questions to Ecuadorans including whether they support the naming of Alarcon as president. He told local television that if voters approve, "a new, stronger Ecuador will come out of it. Then there will be nobody who can criticise or interpret what happened in February ... there will be a solid government that will be able to face Ecuador's problems with vigour."

Congress dismissed President Abdala Bucaram in February on grounds of mental incompetence and named Alarcon as interim president until elections are held in the middle of 1998. Some observers, including Bucaram, questioned the legality of Alarcon's appointment without an election.

"Instead of criticising some sectors of the legislature, critics should be thankful for having a clear view of the will of the people" through the poll, Alarcon said. The poll, which he announced in an address to the nation on Sunday, will not be binding on the government.
It will also ask voters if they approve constitutional changes to the legal and electoral systems.
